subject: Helix Pilot: capacity readiness, GPU shortlist & benchmark plan
messages:
From: Jared Sanders <jared.sanders@helixhealth.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Malhotra <p.malhotra@helixhealth.ai>, infra@helixhealth.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's SLO/discovery call

Thanks for the call this morning — good context. A few clarifying points from our side so we can align the pilot expectations:

- Target workload: clinical note summarization + synchronous chat (streaming) for internal clinical users. Expected average request length 300 tokens, peak 1,200 tokens for some long notes.
- Traffic profile: steady 35 rps during office hours, spiky up to 120 rps for short bursts (30–45s).
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end for interactive chat should be <= 250ms for the first 64 tokens and stream remaining tokens without blocking UX.
- Throughput SLO: sustain 12K tokens/sec reserved throughput during peak windows.
- Availability: need 99.9% during business hours; offline batch acceptable overnight.

We'd like Redwood to propose a concrete dedicated capacity configuration (GPU mix, reserved throughput, concurrency) and a short benchmark plan we can run with our infra team next week. Also share any quantization/precision notes (FP16 vs int8) that might impact output fidelity for clinical terminology.

Jared
Director, Product Infrastructure
Helix Health

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Jared Sanders <jared.sanders@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's SLO/discovery call

Jared — appreciate the clear workload breakdown. High-level response and proposed next steps below. Attaching a draft SLO matrix and an initial GPU shortlist.

Summary of our read: 
- Observed requirement balance: low interactive tail-latency for first-token + high sustained token throughput for summarization. That typically favors a mixed approach: a lower-latency instance class for interactive sessions (fewer tokens, lower batch sizes) and a high-throughput instance pool for bulk summarization.

Preliminary GPU shortlist (for pilot):
- H100 80GB FP16: strongest raw latency and throughput for large batches; good for high concurrency streaming when using optimized kernels.
- A100 80GB FP16: predictable latency, strong throughput for longer contexts, more available in clouds.
- L40s (mixed precision, 48GB): cost-effective for quantized int8/4-bit serving if output quality acceptable after eval.

Proposed pilot benchmark plan (90–96 hour window):
1) Micro-latency profile: p50/p95/p99 first-token latency with realistic 300-token requests, streaming enabled, concurrency ramps 1→64.
2) Sustained throughput run: continuous generation at target token/sec (12K tokens/sec) for 2 hours on candidate GPU; measure memory pressure, kernel stalls, and QoS tail.
3) Burst tolerance: short 60s spike test to 120 rps to validate autoscaling/burst capacity and fallback behavior.
4) Fidelity vs quantization: run paired evals (FP16 vs int8/4-bit) on a clinical prompt set to measure semantic F1 and safety regressions.

Deliverables from Redwood for the pilot:
- Config recommendations (reserved tokens/sec, concurrency per instance, batching window) per GPU class
- Bench harness + scripts, Docker images, and a short runbook for your infra to execute
- Pre-filled pilot SLO matrix with pass/fail criteria and tooling to collect p95/p99, jitter, and CPU/GPU metrics

Requested from Helix:
- A 100-example prompt/eval set with clinical highlights (we'll use for fidelity checks)
- Cloud region preference and any compliance constraints (KMS/HSM)

Next steps: I can circulate a formal runbook and schedule a 30m pilot kickoff for Monday. Does 10am PT work for your infra team?

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: helix_pilot_slo_matrix.xlsx; gpu_shortlist_comparison.pdf

From: Priya Malhotra <p.malhotra@helixhealth.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Jared Sanders <jared.sanders@helixhealth.ai>, infra@helixhealth.ai
Date: 2027-12-02T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Helix Pilot: capacity readiness, GPU shortlist & benchmark plan

Thanks Aditya — Monday 10am PT works. A few clarifications from infra: 

- Region: us-west-2 preferred. We have reserved instances and can try a pilot there.
- Security: we'll need KMS integration and the runbook steps for key rotation documented.
- For burst capacity, we want to understand graceful degradation: if reserved pool saturates, can you route to a lower-cost quantized pool and surface a degradation header so our client can show a degraded-quality indicator?

Also, can you provide an initial sizing recommendation in tokens/sec per GPU so we can map to our reserved instance limits? Example: how many tokens/sec can an A100 80GB with FP16 sustain at 95th-percentile <200ms for 300-token mean requests?

Priya
Infra Lead, Helix Health

On Dec 1, 2027, at 16:12, aditya_rao@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jared — appreciate the clear workload breakdown. High-level response and proposed next steps below. Attaching a draft SLO matrix and an initial GPU shortlist.

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Priya Malhotra <p.malhotra@helixhealth.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-03T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Helix Pilot: capacity readiness, GPU shortlist & benchmark plan

Priya — quick answers and the bench numbers we'll validate during the run: 

Sizing guidance (initial estimates; pilot to validate):
- H100 80GB (FP16): ~5.5K–7.5K tokens/sec sustained per card for 300-token mean requests at p95 first-token latency ~80–140ms depending on batching window and instance concurrency. Better for mixed workloads when you lean on optimized kernels + CUDA graphing.
- A100 80GB (FP16): ~3.5K–5K tokens/sec sustained per card for the same profile; p95 first-token latency ~120–220ms. More predictable but lower peak throughput versus H100.
- L40s (int8/4-bit quantized): ~6K–9K tokens/sec per card for bulk summarization if quantization artefacts acceptable; first-token p95 can be similar or slightly worse for small-batch streaming without KV-cache tuning.

Notes on graceful degradation and routing: 
- Yes — we can implement policy-based routing: primary path to reserved FP16 pool; fallback to quantized pool if utilization crosses threshold (we'll surface a degradation flag and confidence score). That requires a short eval window in pilot to calibrate quality thresholds.

Pilot logistics & next actions: 
1) Kickoff Mon 10am PT — run through runbook and tagging + KMS steps (Aditya + Marcus + Karhtik + Helix infra)
2) Helix: share the 100 clinical prompts + region credentials by EOD Friday so we can pre-stage images in us-west-2.
3) Redwood: deliver bench harness and a pre-populated SLO matrix by Monday morning (we'll include sample graph dashboards + alerts).
4) Run schedule: day 1 micro-latency + concurrency ramp; day 2 sustained throughput + burst tests; day 3 quantization fidelity checks + report.

I'll attach a short runbook and a trimmed GPU comparison table to the Drive link after this note. If any of the timing constraints don't work, flag them and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
